title: Normalization projective components
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field] and $C$ a projective $k$-scheme [def-pc-scheme, def-kun-projective]. Let $N\to C$ be the normalization, meaning the disjoint union of the normalizations [def-sc-normalization] of the reduced irreducible components [def-weil-irreducible-components, def-weil-pbc-scheme-reduction, lem-weil-pbc-reduced-induced-closed-subscheme, lem-weil-pbc-scheme-coproduct-family]. Then $N\to C$ is finite and surjective [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], $N$ is projective and proper over $k$, and $N=\coprod_{i\in I}N_i$ for a finite set $I$, where each $N_i$ is nonempty, normal (every local ring is an integrally closed domain), integral and both open and closed in $N$ [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring, def-pc-integral-scheme, def-weil-open-immersion]. Each $N_i$ is projective and proper over $k$. If $\dim C\le1$ [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension], then $\dim N_i\le1$ for all $i$. The map $N\to C$ factors through $C_{\mathrm{red}}$ as its normalization. The set $I$ is empty if and only if $C$ is empty.

source.place: Tags 0BXR (lemma-normalization-locally-algebraic), 0GK4 (lemma-normalize-projective), 033M (properties.tex, lemma-normal-Noetherian); dimension via Tags 00OK (algebra.tex, lemma-integral-sub-dim-equal) and 00OY (algebra.tex, lemma-Noether-normalization)

proof.text: By [lem-pc-projective-proper], the structure map $C\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ is proper. Properness includes finite type and quasi-compactness [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions]. Since the base $\operatorname{Spec}k$ is affine, its inverse image $C$ is quasi-compact [def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme]. The field $k$ is Noetherian: its only ideals are $0$ and $k$. Thus $\operatorname{Spec}k$ is locally Noetherian [pqf-def-locnoeth], and [pqf-lem-locnoeth-lft] makes $C$ locally Noetherian. Together with quasi-compactness this says that $C$ is Noetherian. Apply [lem-sc-noetherian-closed-subset-finite-components] with $E=C$ to get a finite set $I$ of its irreducible components whose union is $C$.

source.place: Tag 0BXR (lemma-normalization-locally-algebraic), proof: Noetherianity and finiteness of irreducible components; inputs 01WC, 01T6, 0BA8

proof.text: Give each component $Z_i$ its reduced induced closed subscheme structure using [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-induced-closed-subscheme]. It is nonempty and irreducible by [def-weil-irreducible-components], and reduced by the cited construction; hence it is integral by the equivalence in [def-pc-integral-scheme]. Its inclusion $a_i:Z_i\to C$ is a closed immersion and therefore finite by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-finite]. Apply [lem-fin-finite-over-projective] to $S=\operatorname{Spec}k$, $T=C$, $h=a_i$: the base is Noetherian as checked in step 1 and is affine. Use the revised lemma's affine-base conclusion (take $U=S$), which supplies a closed immersion into $\mathbf P^N_k$ and hence makes $Z_i$ projective over $k$. By [lem-pc-projective-proper], it is proper and hence of finite type over $k$.

source.place: Tag 0BXR and section-normalization, componentwise construction; Schemes 01J3/01J4; Morphisms 035C, 0B3I and 0C4P

proof.text: Choose the generic point $\eta_i$ of $Z_i$ by [lem-sc-scheme-sober], and put $K=\mathcal O_{Z_i,\eta_i}$. By [lem-sc-integral-function-field-affine-fraction], each nonempty affine open $U=\operatorname{Spec}A$ of $Z_i$ has $A$ a domain with fraction field $K=k(Z_i)$. By the affine description in [def-fin-normalization-extension] applied to $L=K$, which identifies this construction with [def-sc-normalization], its inverse image in $N_i$ is $\operatorname{Spec}\overline A$, the integral closure of $A$ in $K$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-integral-closure-finite-extension-normal] to the degree-one extension $K/K$: $\overline A$ is a normal domain with fraction field $K$. For a point of this affine chart corresponding to a prime $\mathfrak q$, [lem-weil-pbc-spec-domain-stalks-function-field] identifies its structure-sheaf stalk with $\overline A_{\mathfrak q}$. The stalk in this open chart equals the stalk in $N_i$, since neighborhoods contained in the chart are cofinal among all neighborhoods of the point. This prime localization is a normal domain by [lem-weil-pbc-localization-normal-domain], so every local ring of $N_i$ is an integrally closed domain. These affine charts also prove integrality. In each chart, the zero prime of $\overline A$ maps to the zero prime of $A$, hence to $\eta_i$. It is the only prime over $\eta_i$: if a prime $\mathfrak q\subset\overline A$ contracts to zero and contains a nonzero $b$, write $b=a/s$ in $K=\operatorname{Frac}(A)$ with $a,s\in A$ nonzero; then $a=sb\in\mathfrak q\cap A$, a contradiction. Every nonempty affine open of $Z_i$ contains $\eta_i$ by [lem-sc-integral-function-field-affine-fraction]. Consequently every point over $\eta_i$ belongs to every one of these inverse-image charts. Their zero primes therefore represent one and the same point of $N_i$, the unique point over $\eta_i$. Every point belongs to a chart and is a specialization of that generic point, so $N_i$ is irreducible. Its affine charts are reduced since their rings are domains, and it is nonempty by step 3. Thus the equivalence in [def-pc-integral-scheme] gives that $N_i$ is integral.

source.place: Tag 035Q (lemma-normalization-normal), clause (1), written on integral-component affine charts; Algebra 034L and 00GY; affine description: blueprint sec-curve-estimates/sk-prop-cd-affine/def-fin-normalization-extension.md, L=K; stalk identification: Schemes 01HV (lemma-spec-sheaves), clause (6)

proof.text: The normalization in the statement is $N=\coprod_{i\in I}N_i$. By [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-coproduct-family], each coprojection identifies $N_i$ with an open and closed subscheme, and these images are disjoint and cover $N$. The maps $a_i\nu_i:N_i\to C$ induce the stated map $\nu:N\to C$. It is finite: enumerate the finite set $I$ and inductively apply [lem-weil-pbc-finite-coproduct] to the finite maps of step 3. In the empty-family base case the inverse image of any affine $\operatorname{Spec}R$ is $\varnothing=\operatorname{Spec}0$, and $0$ is generated as an $R$-module by the empty list, so the map is finite by [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism]. It is surjective: each point of $C$ lies in a component $Z_i$ by step 1 and has a preimage in $N_i$ by step 3.

source.place: Tag 0BXR, clause (1); Morphisms 0CYI (lemma-finite-union-finite), including the empty case explicitly

proof.text: Apply [lem-fin-finite-over-projective] over the Noetherian base $\operatorname{Spec}k$ first to the finite map $\nu:N\to C$ of step 5 and then to each finite map $a_i\nu_i:N_i\to C$ of step 3. The base $S=\operatorname{Spec}k$ is affine, so in each application take the affine open $U=S$ in the revised lemma. Its affine-base conclusion supplies a global closed embedding over $k$ for $N$ and for each $N_i$. Since $C$ is projective, this proves that $N$ and every $N_i$ are projective over $k$. Applying [lem-pc-projective-proper] to these structure morphisms proves that all of them are proper over $k$.

source.place: Tag 0GK4 (lemma-normalize-projective), proof: finite over projective and projective implies proper

proof.text: The reduction $C_{\mathrm{red}}\to C$ is the identity on underlying spaces by [def-weil-pbc-scheme-reduction], so it has exactly the same irreducible components. Every $Z_i$ is reduced. Therefore [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-source-factors-through-closed-subscheme] factors $a_i$ through $C_{\mathrm{red}}$. Explicitly, on $\operatorname{Spec}R\subset C$ its component is cut out by a radical ideal $J_i$, and $\sqrt{(0)}\subseteq J_i$; its map to the reduction is induced by $R/\sqrt{(0)}\to R/J_i$. The reduced induced structure on the same closed subset of $C_{\mathrm{red}}$ is again $\operatorname{Spec}(R/J_i)$, by the affine description and uniqueness in [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-induced-closed-subscheme]. Thus the component normalizations used to construct $N$ are exactly those of $C_{\mathrm{red}}$. Their maps induce $N\to C_{\mathrm{red}}$ by the coproduct mapping property [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-coproduct-family], and its composite with $C_{\mathrm{red}}\to C$ is $\nu$, since this equality holds on each summand. This is the normalization of $C_{\mathrm{red}}$ in the componentwise meaning stipulated in the statement.

source.place: Tag 035O (lemma-normalization-reduced); affine componentwise argument using Schemes 01J3 and 0356

proof.text: Suppose $\dim C\le1$. A chain of irreducible closed subsets of the closed subspace $Z_i$ is also a chain of irreducible closed subsets of $C$, with the same strict inclusions. By [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension], $\dim Z_i\le\dim C$. Combine this with the equality $\dim N_i=\dim Z_i$ already supplied by [lem-sc-normalization-exists] in step 3 to obtain $\dim N_i\le1$.

source.place: Tag 0GK5 (lemma-dim-1-projective-completion-after-insep), use of normalized projective components; dimension equality from the existing normalization lemma

proof.text: If $I$ is empty, the components' union in step 1 is empty and hence $C$ is empty. Conversely, if $C$ is empty there is no nonempty irreducible subset, hence no irreducible component by [def-weil-irreducible-components], so $I$ is empty. In this case $N$ is the empty coproduct and the claims about individual $N_i$ are vacuous.
